8088 Instructions

The reduced Intel 8088 instruction set that the interpreter runs. Instructions that are not on this page are not supported.

Program structure

  • Constants go at the beginning, in the form NAME = value. The system call constants (_EXIT, _GETCHAR, _PRINTF) are not predefined: the program must define them.
  • .SECT .TEXT contains the instructions. Execution starts from the first instruction of this section: the main: label is not required.
  • .SECT .DATA contains data with an initial value. .SECT .BSS contains free space.
  • A label is name:, alone on a line or before an instruction.
  • Comments start with // or with ;.
  • The program ends with the EXIT system call, with HLT, or after the last instruction.

Instructions, directives and registers work in upper or lower case (MOV AX, 5 or mov ax, 5). Labels and constants are case-sensitive.

Examples for your first run

Create a .a8088 file, copy an example into the file and click Run or Debug.

1. Hello, World!

hello.a8088
_EXIT = 1
_PRINTF = 127

.SECT .TEXT
    PUSH 0              // value (this format does not use it)
    PUSH msg            // address of the format string
    PUSH _PRINTF
    SYS                 // SYS pops 127, the format and the value off the stack
    PUSH 0              // exit code
    PUSH _EXIT
    SYS

.SECT .DATA
msg: .ASCII "Hello, World!\n\0"

Output: Hello, World!

2. Input and output

The program reads a number ending with ; and prints twice the number.

double.a8088
_EXIT = 1
_GETCHAR = 117
_PRINTF = 127

.SECT .TEXT
    MOV BX, 0           // BX = number read
read:
    PUSH _GETCHAR
    SYS                 // AL = next input character
    CMPB AL, 59         // 59 = ';' ends the number
    JE done
    SUBB AL, 48         // ASCII digit -> value
    XORB AH, AH
    MOV CX, AX          // CX = digit
    MOV AX, BX          // AX = BX * 10
    ADD AX, AX
    MOV DX, AX
    ADD AX, AX
    ADD AX, AX
    ADD AX, DX
    ADD AX, CX          // AX = BX * 10 + digit
    MOV BX, AX
    JMP read
done:
    MOV AX, BX
    ADD AX, BX          // AX = 2 * number
    PUSH AX
    PUSH fmt
    PUSH _PRINTF
    SYS
    PUSH 0
    PUSH _EXIT
    SYS

.SECT .DATA
fmt: .ASCII "%d\n\0"

Input 123; → output 246. Type the input in the terminal and press Enter.

3. Subroutine with CALL and RET

square.a8088
_EXIT = 1
_PRINTF = 127

.SECT .TEXT
    PUSH 7              // argument
    CALL square
    ADD SP, 2           // removes the argument
    PUSH AX
    PUSH fmt
    PUSH _PRINTF
    SYS
    PUSH 0
    PUSH _EXIT
    SYS

square:                 // AX = argument * argument
    PUSH BP
    MOV BP, SP
    MOV AX, [BP+4]      // [BP+2] = return address, [BP+4] = argument
    MUL AL              // AX = AL * AL
    POP BP
    RET

.SECT .DATA
fmt: .ASCII "7 * 7 = %d\n\0"

Output: 7 * 7 = 49. In Debug, the STACK shows the words of square in a group with its name.

Data transfer

InstructionOperandsDescription
MOVdest, srcCopies src into dest.
MOVBdest, srcCopies a byte. Registers must be 8-bit. In memory it writes a single byte.
PUSHsrcPushes a word onto the stack: SP decreases by 2.
POPdestPops a word off the stack and copies it into dest: SP increases by 2.

Arithmetic

InstructionOperandsDescription
ADDdest, srcdest = dest + src.
ADDBdest, srcSum of two bytes.
ADCdest, srcdest = dest + src + CF.
SUBdest, srcdest = dest - src.
SUBBdest, srcSubtraction of two bytes.
SBBdest, srcdest = dest - src - CF.
CMPop1, op2Computes op1 - op2 and sets the flags. The operands do not change.
CMPBop1, op2Like CMP, on two bytes.
MULsrcAX = AL * src, truncated to 16 bits. DX does not change.
MULBsrcAX = AL * src, with an 8-bit src. The result goes into AH:AL.
DIVsrcDivides AX by src: quotient in AL, remainder in AH. DX is not part of the dividend. A quotient greater than 255 loses its high bits. Division by zero stops the program with an error.
DIVBsrcDivides AL by src (8-bit): quotient in AL, remainder in AH. The initial value of AH does not matter.
INCdestdest = dest + 1. CF does not change.
DECdestdest = dest - 1. CF does not change.

Logic

InstructionOperandsDescription
ANDdest, srcBitwise AND. CF = 0.
ORdest, srcBitwise OR. CF = 0.
XORdest, srcBitwise XOR. CF = 0. XOR AX, AX sets AX to zero.
XORBdest, srcBitwise XOR of two bytes.
NOTdestInverts every bit. Does not change the flags.

Jumps and subroutines

Use jumps after a CMP. "Signed" means the values are in two's complement.

InstructionOperandsJumps if
JMPlabelAlways.
JE / JZlabelEqual: ZF = 1.
JNE / JNZlabelNot equal: ZF = 0.
JL / JNGElabelLess, signed: SF ≠ OF.
JLE / JNGlabelLess or equal, signed: ZF = 1 or SF ≠ OF.
JG / JNLElabelGreater, signed: ZF = 0 and SF = OF.
JGE / JNLlabelGreater or equal, signed: SF = OF.
JB / JNAE / JClabelBelow, unsigned: CF = 1.
JBE / JNAlabelBelow or equal, unsigned: CF = 1 or ZF = 1.
JA / JNBElabelAbove, unsigned: CF = 0 and ZF = 0.
JAE / JNB / JNClabelAbove or equal, unsigned: CF = 0.
JS / JNSlabelSF = 1 / SF = 0.
JO / JNOlabelOF = 1 / OF = 0.
JP / JPElabelEven parity: PF = 1.
JNP / JPOlabelOdd parity: PF = 0.
JCXZlabelCX = 0.
LOOPlabelDecreases CX by 1, then jumps if CX ≠ 0.
CALLlabelAlways. Pushes the address of the next instruction onto the stack.
RET-Pops the return address off the stack and jumps to that address.

System instructions

InstructionOperandsDescription
SYS-System call. SYS pops the call number off the stack and then its arguments: no ADD SP, n is needed after SYS. An unknown number does nothing and leaves the arguments on the stack.
HLT-Stops the program with code 0 and prints Program halted.
NOP-Does nothing.

System calls

NumberNameUsageDescription
1EXITPUSH code
PUSH _EXIT
SYS		Ends the program and prints Program exited with code: N.
117GETCHARPUSH _GETCHAR
SYS		Reads one input character and puts its code (0 to 255) in AL. AH does not change. If the input is empty, the program waits: type the characters in the terminal and press Enter. Enter does not send the newline character.
127PRINTFPUSH value
PUSH format
PUSH _PRINTF
SYS		Prints the format string with a single value. Use %d, %x, %o or %c, only once: two specifiers cause an error. The value is an unsigned word: -1 becomes 65535. The string must end with \0 (at most 256 bytes).

Operands

TypeDescription
16-bit registersAX, BX, CX, DX, SI, DI, BP, SP.
8-bit registersAL, AH, BL, BH, CL, CH, DL, DH. Instructions ending in B (MOVB, ADDB, ...) accept only these registers.
Segment registersCS, DS, ES, SS. All are 0 at the start. CS is read-only.
ImmediatesDecimal (27, -1), hexadecimal (0x1B) and octal with a leading zero, as in C (033 equals 27). 09 is decimal. Characters such as 'A' are not supported: use the code (65).
Labels and constantsloop, msg, _EXIT. label+n, label-n and label1-label2 are also valid.
Memory[BX], [SI], [BP+4], [BP-2], [label], [label+2], [label-1], [label+BX], [BX+SI+2]. The (BX) form is also valid. With BP the address is in the stack segment. The access size is one byte with instructions ending in B or with an 8-bit register (MOV [x], AL), otherwise one word.

Directives

DirectiveExampleDescription
=_EXIT = 1Defines a constant.
.SECT.SECT .TEXTStarts the .TEXT, .DATA or .BSS section.
.ASCIImsg: .ASCII "Hello\n\0"In .DATA: writes the characters of the string, one byte per character. The valid sequences are \0, \n, \t, \r and \\. The string does not get an automatic \0.
.BYTEv: .BYTE 1, 0x2, 03In .DATA: writes one or more bytes.
.SPACEbuf: .SPACE 10In .BSS or in .DATA: reserves n zeroed bytes.

Every line in .DATA and .BSS must have its own label: the interpreter ignores a line without a label. .DATA starts at address 0x1000 and .BSS at address 0x2000. In the MEMORY context each cell is a non-zero byte of these sections. The bytes of a label are in a group with the label's name and address, for example msg (0x1000), and each cell is named after its offset: msg+0, msg+1. A byte outside any label is named after its address.

Flags

FlagNameIs 1 when
ZFZeroThe result is zero.
SFSignThe highest bit of the result is 1 (negative result).
CFCarryThe operation has a carry or a borrow (unsigned).
OFOverflowThe signed result does not fit in the register.
PFParityThe low byte of the result has an even number of 1 bits.

Differences from the real 8088

Interpreter behaviors to be aware of
  • MUL always computes AX = AL * src, even with a 16-bit operand. The real 8088 computes DX:AX = AX * src.
  • DIV always divides AX and puts the quotient in AL. The real 8088, with a 16-bit divisor, divides DX:AX and puts the quotient in AX.
  • MUL and MULB set the flags from the low byte of the result. The real 8088 sets CF = OF = 1 when the high half of the result is not zero.
